questions.question: For the demo image (24, 24, 3) and patch_size=6, what does patchify return?
options: 16 patches, each flattened to 108 values, on a 4×4 grid
24 patches, each 6 values, on a 3×3 grid
4 patches, each 16 values, on a 6×6 grid
16 patches, each 24 values, on a 6×6 grid
questions.explanation: Both spatial dimensions split into 24/6=4 cells, giving 16 patches; each contains 6*6*3=108 channel values.

questions.question: What shape does linear_project produce for those 16 flattened patches with d_model=48?
questions.explanation: The projection maps each 108-value patch to one 48-wide vector while preserving the number of patches.

questions.question: What happens to the sequence length in cls_and_pos for a 4×4 patch grid?
options: It becomes 48 because position vectors are concatenated to every patch
It remains 16 because [CLS] replaces the first patch
It becomes 17 because one learnable [CLS] vector is prepended to 16 patch tokens
It becomes 20 because four row tokens are added
questions.explanation: cls_and_pos starts its output with one CLS vector and then appends every patch after adding its 2D positional encoding.

questions.question: Why does pos_2d require d_model to be divisible by 4?
options: It divides the image into four equal patch grids
It needs four separate class tokens for the image corners
It stores four RGB values at every spatial position
It splits the width into row and column halves, each needing even sin/cos pairs
questions.explanation: Half the dimensions encode rows and half columns; each half is filled with even/odd sinusoidal pairs.

questions.question: Which component supplies the vision-specific tokenization before a standard Transformer encoder?
options: patchify plus linear_project, followed by [CLS] and 2D position information
The decoder cross-attention and a text tokenizer
A recurrent scan over the image's RGB channels
The classifier head before any patch is formed
questions.explanation: The demo makes image patches into token vectors and adds position/CLS information; the later transformer block can reuse an encoder architecture.

questions.question: In param_count_vit, what is counted by `head = d_model * num_classes`?
options: The Q, K, and V projections for every attention head
The final linear classifier that maps the representation to class logits
The number of spatial patches in the input image
The learned [CLS] vector plus all position embeddings
questions.explanation: The classifier head has one output weight per model dimension and class; position and CLS terms are counted separately.
